title: Beyond the Remembered World: Predictive 4D Belief for Persistent Navigation in Evolving Worlds
abstract: arXiv:2609.39166v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Persistent spatial memory enables embodied agents to navigate familiar environments across repeated visits. However, targets may move while unobserved, including during navigation, making remembered locations unreliable by the time an agent arrives. Despite advances in memory retrieval and state prediction, accounting for continued hidden world evolution and revising beliefs under limited visibility remain challenging. We study Evolving-World Navigation, where agents infer target locations from intermittent observations, predict their states at inspection time, and revise beliefs using visual evidence. We propose EvolvingNav, which constructs a time-indexed belief from timestamped 3D object histories through a structured persistence-relocation model. translated_title: 超越被记住的世界：用于演化世界中持久导航的预测性4D信念
translated_abstract: 持久性空间记忆使具身智能体能够在多次访问中导航熟悉的环境。然而，目标可能在未被观察期间（包括导航过程中）发生移动，这使得智能体到达时记忆的位置变得不可靠。尽管在记忆检索和状态预测方面已有进展，但如何考虑持续发生的隐藏世界演化，并在有限可见性条件下修正信念，仍然是一个挑战。我们研究演化世界导航问题，即智能体需要从间歇性观测中推断目标位置，在抵达检查时刻预测其状态，并利用视觉证据修正信念。我们提出EvolvingNav，它通过一个结构化的持久-迁移模型，从带时间戳的3D物体历史中构建时间索引的信念。该信念能够区分目标停留在最后观测位置的持久性与迁移到其他位置的情况，并在已知候选集之外保留概率质量。一个事件驱动的滤波器（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出EvolvingNav框架，通过结构化持久-迁移模型构建时间索引的4D信念，使具身智能体能够在目标可能隐藏移动的演化世界中，结合间歇性观测与视觉证据预测并动态修正目标位置信念，实现更可靠的持久导航。
en_tdlr: EvolvingNav constructs a time-indexed 4D belief via a structured persistence-relocation model, enabling embodied agents to predict target states at inspection time and iteratively revise beliefs with visual evidence for reliable persistent navigation in evolving worlds where targets may move unobserved.
